View Deal Gaming PC Specifications to look for When looking for a new gaming PC, you need to pay special attention to specs. More recent and more powerful components are better, but this increases the overall price of the system. You can sometimes find gaming rigs that have last-generation parts that will still play games well and save some cash. GPU: A choice between Nvidia, AMD, or Intel in your system will determine how well the computer game graphics are displayed on your monitor. Nvidia has the most powerful GPUs, with the likes of the RTX 5090 and RTX 5080, but AMD's RX 9070 XT is also a great mid-range card. See our GPU hierarchy for an idea of GPU performance. CPU: Either AMD or Intel will get the job done, but AMD currently rules the roost in pure gaming benchmarks, with the 9000-series X3D processors providing the best performance. Memory: At a minimum, you'll want 16GB of RAM. Operating systems and browsers can swallow a huge chunk of your available system RAM before you even boot your game. Having 32GB of memory is ideal for gaming if you can splurge. Storage: With the size of AAA games constantly expanding, you ideally want a minimum of 1TB of storage, preferably in the form of a fast M.2 SSD. You can do better than a spinning hard drive. title: Get an RTX 5060 prebuilt for just $750 in deal that seems too good to be true
summary: Walmart has an exceptional deal on an RTX 5060-powered gaming desktop, which is on sale for just $750 right now.
content: Walmart has the ABS Cyclone M Aqua on sale for just $750 , which is a prebuilt that packs an RTX 5060, Core i5-14400F, 16GB of DDR4 memory, and a 1TB SSD. ABS is Newegg's in-house PC brand, and yet Walmart is the only retailer where we found this deal. Check out the ABS Cyclone M Aqua at Walmart Just about any gaming PC you find under $1,000 has some serious compromises given the ongoing RAM, SSD, and GPU pricing crisis's. And this machine too has compromises, notably with the mATX motherboard and single 16GB DDR4-3200 DIMM. You're getting a lot for the money even with those compromises between the Core i5-14400F and RTX 5060, however. As you can see from our roundup of the best Black Friday gaming PC deals , there aren't a ton of options at this price. And in our tracking of Black Friday GPU deals , we found that the RTX 5060 is selling for close to $500 in many cases. Cyclone M Aqua (RTX 5060, Core i5-14400F, 16GB DDR4, 1TB SSD): was $1399.99 now $749 The ABS Cyclone M Aqua is an mATX prebuilt with an RTX 5060, Core i5-14400F, 16GB of DDR4, and a 1TB NVMe SSD. View Deal As you can see from the data from our GPU benchmark hierarchy , the RTX 5060 is a graphics card that's most comfortable at 1080p, though it can scale up to 1440p, assuming you're willing to lean into Nvidia's DLSS suite between Super Resolution and Multi-Frame Generation, both of which are supported on this GPU. Future Tom's Hardware Its main limitation is the 8GB frame buffer, which could pose issues in some titles at 1440p. For the vast majority of 1080p games, it shouldn't be a problem. In our testing of DLSS 5 , which is supported on the RTX 5060, we found that the 8GB frame buffer posed a limitation on performance. However, Nvidia has already apparently slashed the VRAM usage of its DLSS 5 model. The RTX 5060 was fast enough to reach 58 FPS at 1080p with DLSS 5 still. Outside of the GPU, the Core i5-14400F is the perfect CPU for a rig like this. It provides performance on the level of the Core i5-14600K in games while sacrificing a bit of peak productivity power and the unlocked multiplier. The one major downside with this configuration is the single 16GB DDR4-3200 DIMM. With just a single stick, your bandwidth is cut in half. Thankfully, the motherboard has four DIMM slots, so you can add another 16GB module to double your capacity and unlock the full bandwidth. Cheapest DDR4 In today's market, memory has become one of the most critical and expensive components in any build, and prices have only worsened thanks to the ongoing global DRAM shortage. We're keeping an eye on the volatile memory pricing to help identify any good deals that may arise. Now, even more so than before the shortage began, price tags are fluctuating significantly from day to day, and it's becoming increasingly complex to tell when you're getting a fair deal versus overpaying for the same memory kit. We've compiled this comprehensive RAM price tracker that monitors the availability and pricing of different DDR5 and DDR4 memory kits across major U.S. retailers. Our goal is to take the guesswork out of memory shopping and help you make an informed purchasing decision. We update this index regularly with the lowest prices available in the U.S. market for each memory kit. Our tracker covers a range of capacities and speeds across both budget and premium brands. We list the lowest price for each available memory kit, regardless of manufacturer, so you see the absolute best deals currently on offer. The general availability of many memory kits is limited, with truly exceptional deals scarce and often selling out within seconds of appearing. High-capacity kits, particularly DDR5, frequently show the most severe stock shortages and price premiums. Therefore, timing and vigilance are especially important when shopping for memory in current times. Whether you're budget-conscious and want the best bang for your buck, or you're building a premium system and want the best RAM for gaming available, our index further below gives you the data you need to make the right purchase. For instance, a conventional 32GB (2x16GB) DDR5-6000 memory kit sold for around $100 to $200 in October 2025, but the same kit now starts at $430, if it's even in stock. Retailers are taking advantage of the DRAM shortage, just as they did with the graphics card shortage a few years ago. They've started raising DDR5 prices to align with current market conditions and sometimes bundle DDR5 memory kits with processor or motherboard purchases. title: 7 new Intel Nova Lake-S Core Ultra 4000-series CPUs detailed in new leak
summary: A number of new, unannounced Intel Core Ultra 4000-series chips have been detailed in a Nova Lake document, ahead of what is expected to be an official unveiling of the chips at a next-generation desktop chip event in Berlin, Germany, in February 2027.
content: A newly leaked document purportedly details no less than seven new Nova Lake-S desktop processors based on C1 stepping qualification samples, including 28-core models, three months before Intel is expected to officially take the wraps off them. The new leak, from VideoCardz , includes an Intel warning that clock speeds and performance may change before the final products are ready to be shipped. But given the fact that this rarely happens when dealing with qualification samples, it's believed that the chips will likely be released just as they are outlined in the document, if the leak is accurate. Of the seven chips that have been detailed, the top-of-the-line Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC will be the one of most interest. It will reportedly feature 28 cores comprising eight performance cores, 16 efficiency cores, and four low-power efficient cores. Its base efficiency core clock speed of 2.7 GHz is eclipsed by the 5.5 GHz boost speed its performance cores will reach, while 144 MB of L3 cache and a 125-watt power rating round out the main figures. According to the leak, it will be joined by a Core Ultra 9 4950K with the same core count and almost identical clock speeds, albeit with a much smaller 36 MB L3 cache. Beyond that, the report says the Core 9 4900 BFC will be locked at 65 watts, have 22 cores, and a 120 MB L3 cache. If the leak holds up, the mid-range will be catered for by the Core Ultra 7 4870K and 4850K chips. Both will reportedly have a 125-watt power rating and 24 cores, but will again differ in terms of L3 cache — the former will have 144 MB, the latter just 36 MB. Both will boost to 5.2 GHz. The report says the entry-level models will include the Core Ultra 5 4650K and 4650KF, both packing 22 cores and 30 MB L3 caches, and that they'll also have the same 125-watt power rating and top out at a boosted 5.1 GHz, according to the documentation. The specs also indicate a maximum of 256 GB of RAM is supported, with 24 CPU PCIe lanes and a 77 PTOPS integrated NPU. Integrated graphics are set to range from 2.9 to 3.1 GHz depending on the chosen chip, with support for the DNx, XAVC, JPEG-XS, and VVC decoding all included alongside AV1 High and Professional profile support. It has previously been reported that Intel is likely to announce its next-gen chips at an event in Berlin, Germany, between February 22 and 25, 2026. But we can also expect that motherboard manufacturers will show off products compatible with the new chips before that — no doubt at the CES 2027 event in Las Vegas in January. It's already been confirmed that new motherboards will be needed if you plan on picking up any of the next-gen chips. This latest leak comes weeks after it was reported that the new Nova Lake chips would "universally limit the maximum core frequency to 5.1 GHz when above 90°C." However, it's important to remember that the limitation only applies when the chips reach that temperature. Machines with adequate cooling will not experience that limitation, although it remains to be seen how easy these chips are to cool.

title: Resourceful PC owner repurposes CPU watercooler with dead pump as standalone LCD hardware monitor, vibecodes new software for module
summary: The Redditor salvaged the LCD and controller board, 3D-printed a stand, and used AI to develop a custom software to turn the screen into a standalone PC monitoring display.
content: AIO liquid coolers are notorious for shorter lifespans due to pump failure or leaks, which usually results in having to replace the entire unit. However, one enthusiast decided to salvage theirs uniquely, at least a part of it. Sharing their DIY project on Reddit, u/BodeeHav repurposed the LCD screen from a dead NZXT Kraken AIO into a standalone desktop monitor that displays live CPU and GPU temperatures and utilization after vibecoding entirely new software. According to the post, the pump on their NZXT Kraken AIO stopped working around a month ago. Rather than discarding a perfectly usable screen, they decided to dismantle the block and remove the LCD and its main board. They used the original black outer housing and 3D printed a stand to hold the LCD in place. To keep things tidy, they stripped the connector down to just its SATA power and USB pins. The display connects directly to the motherboard, presumably using the internal 9-pin USB header, although BodeeHav says they plan to adapt it for external USB. Repurposed my dead NZXT Kraken AIO screen into a desktop temp monitor from r/pcmasterrace Getting the display working properly required more than just pulling it out of the pump block. BodeeHav initially used NZXT’s CAM software; however, he kept running into issues whenever the PC entered sleep or standby. To overcome this hurdle, they turned to AI and vibe coded an entirely new software as a replacement that offers full control of the LCD with various customization options. BodeeHav has graciously made his entire project available on GitHub, where you can access the DesktopKraken software and an STL file for the stand. According to the official GitHub page, the software is a standalone Windows application that communicates with compatible NZXT Kraken Elite LCDs over USB without requiring NZXT CAM. The software currently only offers support for the 2023 Kraken Elite and 2024 Kraken Elite V2 , which use circular LCDs with a 640x640 resolution. Apart from CPU and GPU temperatures and utilization, it can also display clock speeds, power consumption, memory usage, and VRAM information. Additionally, the software can be used for brightness control, screen orientation, sensor logging, and it even offers support for custom images, animated GIFs, thermal warning gauges, and automatic recovery after Windows sleep or a USB disconnect. While it may cater to a very niche audience, the project is a great example of how a little ingenuity can give failed components a second life.

title: Razer China partners up with Durex for a limited-edition kit of mousepad and condoms
summary: Razer China partners up with Durex for a limited-edition kit of mousepad and condoms — Long-Lasting Battle Armor meets Heavy Armored Beetle
content: Razer, the brand best-known for its gaming peripherals and laptops, has another quirky collaboration. This time around, the Singapore-American company managed to squeeze in a partnership with Durex for a limited-edition pack of a Razer Goliath mousepad with two Razer-branded Durex Performa delay condoms. Work hard, game harder - Razer x Durex (China exclusive) https://t.co/3iPBFRQGyF November 24, 2026 Before everyone gets too excited, this partnership is specific to the China region. Prospective gamers hoping for a bit of extra after-match fun can reportedly get their hands on the package in two ways: as post-purchase gifts at the Razer or Durex stores on JD.com, or at Tmall's Durex store via redeeming points or as a special offer during live-stream events. There will also be a giveaway held on Dec. 7, though no further details were provided. There's a lot of inter-cultural play in this promotion , as the Goliathus mouse pad is named Heavy Armored Beetle in China (重装甲虫), while the specific Durex condom variant is 持久战甲, roughly "long-lasting battle armor," or protection — plus, both contain the armor/shell symbol 甲. The doubles fun continues with "DLS", as it can be read as "take Razer" (Dài Léishé) or the local pronunciation of Durex, Dùlěisī. The partnership's slogan is "for gaming, bring Razer; for romance, bring Durex." 遂にゲーミングコンドーム登場RazerとDurexがまさかのコラボらしい※中国限定 https://t.co/k6gY1k10SS October 23, 2026 Razer and Durex may stand out as quite the odd couple, but the condom maker has been a sponsor of the Chinese League of Legends Pro League since 2023. Meanwhile, Razer is no stranger to quirky collaborations, as we've seen Razer Gillette razors, Razer-Panerai watches, sneakers, pickleball paddles , Dolce & Gabbana-branded headsets, and even tea. The younger Chinese demographic is reportedly more open to this type of initiative, with unconventional branding pairings having good market uptake. Online commenters were quick to exercise their proverbial mouths, questioning if the target gamer demographics would have a use for the condoms to begin with, and some suggested the decision to offer only two per pack was probably wise. Some outlets were cracking jokes about RGB lighting on the rubbers, too.

title: US Treasury information chief spent three days vibecoding Civilization game clone amidst Treasury database hack
summary: Legatum, a vibecoded browser-based Civilization clone by the US Treasury's own CIO is getting constant updates while the Treasury faces a cybersecurity issue.
content: Someone’s vibecoding a Civilization clone, and it’s the US Treasury’s own Chief Information Officer, Sam Corcos. Some Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) systems and services have been taken offline while the bureau investigates a “cybersecurity incident”; meanwhile, Corcos’ Legatum GitHub repository has been regularly updated for the past three days as his AI agents receive instructions to build it. In an X post earlier this month, Sam Corcos supported the General Services Administration (GSA) mandate, requiring federal workers in the office to send regular updates about what they worked on, which many criticize as micromanagement and authoritarian. Ironically, people are micromanaging Corcos instead, calling him out for spending time on his vibecoded GitHub project instead of working on the Treasury cybersecurity incident. I believe it is reasonable to ask employees what they are working on. In the private sector, we call this a daily standup. November 10, 2026 Legatum , Corcos’ vibecoded browser-based Civilization game clone, reached version 0.1.0 just three days ago. “A historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization.” is Legatum’s tagline, and it’s not ashamed of it. While the repository is likely being updated by Corcos’ Claude and Codex agents, it’s funny how the repository has seen more frequent updates than the situation over at FinCEN. Catherine Rampell on X reports that FinCEN’s Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) batch filing system has been offline for over 24 hours, requiring financial institutions to file reports manually, one at a time. Catherine Rampell further questions Legatum’s development, asking, “I would want to find out who is paying for Corcos’s Claude credits to work on his Civilization game clone. Is it US taxpayers, via Treasury?” The Treasury CIO appears to have spent the past three days vibecoding a Civilization game clone instead of working on this major Treasury database cyber breach. As I type this, his Claude code is literally adding theme music https://t.co/KzWzkKnshS November 25, 2026 While this is Corcos’ personal project, Kyle Pomykala on X replied to Catherine Rampell, jokingly assuring readers that he has raised an issue on the Legatum repository, stating, “The Treasury Department is being hacked, and you are vibecoding a video game instead.” Other GitHub users have replied under the issue with their own jokes, with one even stating Corcos will likely also vibecode the Treasury cybersecurity issue. Eight hours after the ticket was opened, Claude closed it, referring the commenters to the Legatum repository Code of Conduct with no personal response from Corcos.

title: Lawsuit alleges Trump strong-armed Intel
summary: The president apparently threatened the Intel board with "consequences" if they did not accept his demand for a 10% stake on the company.
content: An Intel shareholder lawsuit against the company has revealed the extent to which President Donald Trump is allegedly willing to bend companies to his will. Richard Paisner sued the chipmaker earlier this year, saying that the White House’s 10% stake in exchange for the release of the previously granted CHIPS Act funds was unlawful. Now, Wired viewed unsealed documents from the case that allegedly showed how the president used his influence and position to strong-arm Intel’s board into accepting the deal. Intel was already suffering from financial woes since July 2024, and its new CEO, Lip-Bu Tan, was facing scrutiny over his links to Chinese tech companies . Trump himself has called for Tan’s resignation in August 2025, calling him “highly conflicted.” The Intel chief eventually went to the White House and personally talked to the president, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. It was during this conversation that Trump said that he cooked up the 10% Intel deal. Intel was still waiting on $8.9 billion in funding from the U.S. government through the CHIPS and Science Act, but the White House allegedly wanted something in return. The president quoted himself to the Wall Street Journal telling Lip-Bu Tan, “You know what? I think the United States should be given 10% of Intel,” to which the Intel chief replied, “I would consider that.” Court documents reveal how much pressure Intel’s leadership faced at that time. Internal notes show that a call between the company and Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro had the latter tell the former’s chief financial officer not to make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” and that “the president is expecting to announce a deal on Friday.” Furthermore, even though the government official said that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” it was also noted, “that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.” Because of this, Paisner and his attorney said in the complaint [ PDF ], “In extraordinary and expedited fashion, the Board, operating under the shadow of the President’s threat, and advised by legal counsel that itself was conflicted due to its pro bono promises to the president, caved to the government’s extortion.” Other sources also pointed out that Intel’s external legal counsel provided up to $100 million in free legal services to the Trump administration so it could avoid an executive order that would have prevented it from working with the federal government — something that the White House did to Anthropic after it refused to allow the Pentagon to use Claude for mass domestic surveillance or to control weapons systems. Earlier this week, the president called the Nvidia board to pressure them into reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. This wasn’t the first time that Trump made a deal with the company. The AI chipmaker has previously agreed to pay 15% on its H20 sales to China so that it could be allowed to export them again, followed by an even larger 25% slice on H200 chips in December 2025.
